fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. Right after he says not to let anyone despise Timothy's youth, Paul says, "…but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity." (1 Timothy 4:12). That's five places to lead by example. Paul gives him something to do about it.

Travel and festivals aren't on Paul's list, friend. He says these people will prohibit marriage and require abstinence from certain foods (1 Timothy 4:3). Neither travel nor festivals come up anywhere in these verses. The two things are marriage and certain foods.

That's right, baker. Paul says, "For every creation of God is good…" (1 Timothy 4:4). He goes on to say that nothing received with thanksgiving should be rejected. EVERY creation, friend. That's a big word, and it's the whole point.

Right, baker. Paul says, "By pointing out these things to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus…" (1 Timothy 4:6). Timothy is meant to share them, and he's nourished by the words of faith and sound instruction he has followed. Keeping them to himself isn't in the verse.

Leadership is a fair guess, friend, since Paul left Timothy in Ephesus to do a job (1 Timothy 1:3). But Paul's word here is godliness. He says, "Instead, train yourself for godliness." (1 Timothy 4:7).

Ooh, digging into the past, friend? Paul doesn't go there in this verse. He says, "Let no one despise your youth…" (1 Timothy 4:12). It's Timothy's youth that's on the table, and Paul says what to do about it.

Right, baker. Paul says the gift "…was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders." (1 Timothy 4:14). A prophecy and the elders' hands, both together. Then Paul tells Timothy not to neglect it.

Rewards sound nice, friend, but that's not the word Paul picked. He says, "Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all." (1 Timothy 4:15). Stay at it, and what everybody sees is progress. Like a batch rising in the oven, it shows.
